notes.definition: In the periodic table the elements are arranged in order of atomic (proton) number, so that elements with similar properties are in the same columns, called groups.
explanation: The elements in the periodic table are arranged in order of atomic number, which is the number of protons in each atom. They are also arranged so that elements with similar properties are in the same vertical column, called a group. The horizontal rows are called periods. The table is called a periodic table because similar properties occur at regular intervals: as atomic number increases, a pattern of properties repeats each time a new period starts.

The position of an element is linked to the arrangement of electrons in its atoms. Elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell, which is why they have similar chemical properties. For Groups 1 to 7 the group number equals the number of outer-shell electrons: sodium (2,8,1) is in Group 1 and chlorine (2,8,7) is in Group 7. Group 0 elements, the noble gases, have full outer shells (helium has 2, the others 8), which makes them very unreactive.

The period number equals the number of occupied electron shells. Lithium (2,1), carbon (2,4) and neon (2,8) are all in period 2, so their atoms have two occupied shells. Going across a period, the atomic number increases by one from each element to the next, and one more electron is added to the outer shell. Because the atomic number gives the number of electrons, you can use an element's position to work out its electronic structure, or use its electronic structure to find its position.

Because elements in the same group react in similar ways, you can use the periodic table to predict possible reactions and the probable reactivity of an element from its position. For example, potassium is in the same group as sodium, so it reacts with water to form an alkaline solution and hydrogen, like sodium. Trends within groups also let you predict reactivity: in Group 1 reactivity increases down the group, while in Group 7 it decreases down the group. Metals are found on the left and in the centre of the table, and non-metals on the right.
keyFacts: Elements are arranged in order of atomic (proton) number.
Vertical columns are groups; horizontal rows are periods.
Elements with similar properties are in the same group.
It is called periodic because similar properties occur at regular intervals.
Elements in the same group have the same number of outer-shell electrons, so similar chemical properties.
Group number (Groups 1 to 7) = number of outer-shell electrons.
Period number = number of occupied electron shells.
Group 0 elements have full outer shells and are unreactive.
An element's position can be used to predict its reactions and reactivity.

keyTerms.definition: A table of all the elements arranged in order of atomic number, with elements with similar properties in the same columns.
A vertical column of elements with the same number of outer-shell electrons and similar chemical properties.
A horizontal row of elements whose atoms have the same number of occupied shells.
The number of protons in an atom; elements are placed in order of this number.
Repeating at regular intervals; similar properties recur as atomic number increases.
The highest occupied energy level of an atom; its electrons decide the element's chemical properties.

workedExamples.title: From position to electronic structure
workedExamples.question: An element is in Group 6 and Period 3. Write its electronic structure, find its atomic number and name it.
steps: Period 3 means three occupied shells; Group 6 means 6 electrons in the outer shell.
Inner shells are full, so the structure is 2,8,6.

workedExamples.title: From atomic number to position
workedExamples.question: Potassium has atomic number 19. Find its group and period.

workedExamples.title: Predicting a reaction
workedExamples.question: Bromine is in Group 7 with chlorine. Chlorine reacts with sodium to form sodium chloride. Predict what forms when bromine reacts with sodium.
steps: Bromine and chlorine are in the same group, so both have 7 outer electrons.
Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties, so bromine should react in the same way.
By analogy with sodium chloride, the product is sodium bromide.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the periodic table is arranged in order of relative atomic mass.
misconceptions.right: In fact the modern periodic table is arranged in order of atomic (proton) number.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often mix up groups and periods.
misconceptions.right: In fact groups are vertical columns (same outer electrons) and periods are horizontal rows (same number of shells).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think elements next to each other in a period have similar properties.
misconceptions.right: In fact similar properties are found down a group. Neighbours in a period, such as sodium and magnesium, have different numbers of outer electrons and behave differently.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think Group 0 elements have 0 outer electrons.
misconceptions.right: In fact Group 0 elements have full outer shells (2 for helium, 8 for the others).

realWorld: Chemists searching for new materials use the periodic table to pick elements likely to behave in a similar way to one that already works.
Toxicologists know thallium and cadmium are dangerous partly because they behave like elements the body uses, such as potassium and zinc, which are close by in the table.
The periodic table on the wall of every lab lets scientists predict properties of elements they have never handled, such as the rare element francium.
examTips: Use the periodic table on the data sheet: the smaller number for each element is the atomic number.
When explaining similar properties, say 'same number of electrons in the outer shell', not just 'same group'.
For prediction questions, name a similar element in the same group and describe how it reacts, then apply the trend in reactivity.
Remember Group 0 is on the far right, and group number equals outer electrons only for Groups 1 to 7.
summary: Elements are arranged in order of atomic number.
Groups are columns; periods are rows.
Similar properties recur at regular intervals, hence 'periodic'.
Same group means same number of outer electrons and similar chemical properties.
Group number gives outer electrons; period number gives occupied shells.
Position can be used to predict reactions and reactivity.

questions.question: In what order are the elements arranged in the modern periodic table?
markScheme: 1 mark: atomic (proton) number
questions.explanation: The modern table uses atomic number. Early tables used relative atomic mass, which caused some elements to be in the wrong place.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows an outline of the periodic table.
What name is given to the shaded vertical column labelled X?
markScheme: 1 mark: group
questions.explanation: Columns are groups; rows are periods.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows an outline of the periodic table.
What name is given to the shaded horizontal row labelled Y?
markScheme: 1 mark: period
questions.explanation: A horizontal row is a period. Atoms of elements in the same period have the same number of occupied shells.

questions.question: What do elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of?
markScheme: 1 mark: number of electrons in the outer shell
questions.explanation: Same group means same number of outer electrons. Same number of shells describes a period.

questions.question: Which element has the most similar chemical properties to sodium?
markScheme: 1 mark: potassium
questions.explanation: Potassium is in Group 1 with sodium, so both have 1 outer electron. Magnesium is next to sodium in the period but is in Group 2.

questions.question: Why is the periodic table called 'periodic'?
options: It was invented in a particular period of history
The elements are listed in order of mass
Similar properties occur at regular intervals
All the elements in a period have the same properties
markScheme: 1 mark: similar properties occur at regular intervals
questions.explanation: Periodic means repeating regularly. As atomic number increases, similar properties recur, which is why elements line up in groups.

questions.question: An element has the electronic structure 2,8,2. Which group is it in?
markScheme: 1 mark: Group 2
questions.explanation: The last number, 2, is the number of outer electrons, which equals the group number. This is magnesium.

questions.question: How many occupied electron shells does an atom of an element in Period 3 have?
markScheme: 1 mark: 3
questions.explanation: The period number equals the number of occupied shells. For example, sodium (2,8,1) is in Period 3.

questions.question: Fluorine (atomic number 9) and chlorine (atomic number 17) are in the same group. What is the reason?
options: They have the same number of shells
They both have 7 electrons in their outer shell
They have the same number of protons
markScheme: 1 mark: they both have 7 electrons in their outer shell
questions.explanation: Fluorine is 2,7 and chlorine is 2,8,7. Their numbers of shells and protons differ, but their outer shells both contain 7 electrons.

questions.question: Chlorine reacts with iron to form iron chloride. Which other element is most likely to react with iron in a similar way?
markScheme: 1 mark: bromine
questions.explanation: Bromine is in Group 7 with chlorine, so it has 7 outer electrons and similar chemical properties. Argon is unreactive, and sodium is a metal.

questions.question: Why are the elements in Group 0 very unreactive?
options: They have a full outer shell of electrons
They have only one electron in their outer shell
markScheme: 1 mark: they have a full outer shell of electrons
questions.explanation: Noble gases have full outer shells (2 for helium, 8 for the others), so they do not easily gain, lose or share electrons.

questions.question: Rubidium is in Group 1, below potassium. Which prediction about rubidium is most likely to be correct?
options: It does not react with water
It reacts with water more slowly than sodium
It reacts with water more vigorously than potassium, forming an alkaline solution and hydrogen
It reacts with water to form an acidic solution and oxygen
markScheme: 1 mark: it reacts with water more vigorously than potassium, forming an alkaline solution and hydrogen
questions.explanation: Rubidium has 1 outer electron like the other Group 1 metals, so it reacts the same way, and reactivity increases down Group 1.

questions.question:
An element is in Group 5 of the periodic table.
Give the number of electrons in the outer shell of its atoms.
markScheme: 1 mark: 5
questions.explanation: For Groups 1 to 7, the group number equals the number of outer-shell electrons.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the position of element X in an outline of the periodic table.
The group numbers are shown above the table.
Determine the atomic number of element X.

questions.question:
An element has atomic number 19.
Give the number of the group the element is in.
markScheme: 1 mark: Group 1
questions.explanation: 19 electrons give 2,8,8,1, so there is 1 outer electron: Group 1 (potassium).

questions.question:
An element is in Period 2 and Group 4.
Determine the atomic number of the element.
markScheme: 1 mark: 6
questions.explanation: Period 2 and Group 4 gives the structure 2,4, so there are 6 electrons and 6 protons: carbon.

questions.question:
Calcium has the electronic structure 2,8,8,2
Give the number of the period calcium is in.
markScheme: 1 mark: 4
questions.explanation: There are four occupied shells, so calcium is in Period 4.

questions.question:
Element Q is the element in Period 3 that has a full outer shell.
Determine the atomic number of Q.
markScheme: 1 mark: Q is in Group 0, structure 2,8,8
1 mark: atomic number 18
questions.explanation: A full outer shell means Group 0. In Period 3 this is argon, 2,8,8, with 18 electrons.

questions.question: Describe how the elements are arranged in the periodic table.
markScheme: 1 mark: in order of atomic (proton) number
1 mark: elements with similar properties are in the same columns (groups)
questions.explanation: Both ideas are needed: the order, and grouping similar elements into columns.

questions.question: Explain why the periodic table is called 'periodic'.
markScheme: 1 mark: similar properties occur (repeat) at regular intervals
questions.explanation: Each new period repeats the pattern of the one before, so similar elements fall into columns.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the electronic structures of lithium and sodium.
Explain why lithium and sodium have similar chemical properties.
markScheme: 1 mark: they are both in Group 1
1 mark: both have one electron in their outer shell (Li 2,1; Na 2,8,1)
questions.explanation: Chemical properties depend on outer electrons, so elements with the same number of outer electrons react similarly.

questions.question: Chlorine has atomic number 17. Explain how its position in the periodic table is related to the arrangement of electrons in its atoms.
markScheme: 1 mark: 17 electrons, arranged 2,8,7
1 mark: 7 outer electrons, so Group 7
1 mark: 3 occupied shells, so Period 3
questions.explanation: Atomic number gives the electrons; outer electrons give the group; number of shells gives the period.

questions.explanation: Elements in the same group react in the same way, and the position within the group predicts how reactive they are.

questions.question:
Magnesium has atomic number 12.
Explain how the position of magnesium in the periodic table is related to its atomic number and the arrangement of electrons in its atoms.
markScheme: Indicative content: elements are placed in order of atomic number, so magnesium is the 12th element; atomic number 12 means 12 protons and 12 electrons; electronic structure 2,8,2; 2 outer electrons, so Group 2; three occupied shells, so Period 3; it has similar properties to other Group 2 elements such as calcium, which also have 2 outer electrons.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct electronic structure linked clearly to both group and period, and to atomic number.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): correct group or period, or correct structure, with little explanation.
questions.explanation: The chain of reasoning is: atomic number → electrons → electronic structure → group (outer electrons) and period (shells).

questions.question:
Table 1 shows information about element Z. Z is not one of the first 20 elements.
Use the information in Table 1 to give the position of Z in the periodic table.
Predict, with reasons:
• how Z would react with water and with chlorine
• how the reactivity of Z would compare with sodium and potassium.

rows: Number of electrons in outer shell

markScheme: Indicative content: 1 outer electron so Z is in Group 1; 5 occupied shells so Z is in Period 5 (it is rubidium); elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons and similar chemical properties; so Z should react like sodium and potassium; with water: reacts to form a metal hydroxide (alkaline solution, ZOH) and hydrogen gas, for example fizzing; with chlorine: forms a chloride, ZCl (a white solid/ionic compound); reactivity increases down Group 1; Z is below potassium, so it is more reactive than both sodium and potassium; reaction with water would be very vigorous/violent.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): correct group and period with reasons, sensible predictions for both reactions with products, and a correct reactivity comparison explained by position.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct group with some reasoning, at least one reasonable reaction prediction, and some comparison of reactivity.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): states the group or makes a simple prediction with little reasoning.
questions.explanation: This tests using position to predict: same group means same type of reactions; lower in Group 1 means more reactive.
